questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to stay in Europe and found central Europe very interesting, as I did not have that much knowledge prior to my exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, as the CU Erasmus coordinators were good at providing all info via email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance when i arrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not too difficult but pretty expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should take their time looking. Choose a nice location close to your campus and look at the reviews of the landlord.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very difficult and stressful. The process only started after classes had already begun. Many of the courses i wanted to attend were already full.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was no help available to my knowledge.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I think I got 50% of the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are on a waitlist for a course, you should write an email to the teacher directly. They will most likely let you take the course even if you are on a waiting list.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level differed a lot from course to course. Some had a very high level, and I used a lot of time to prepare for them; other classes had no mandatory reading, and I did not have to prepare for them at all.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was more discussion-based. I had almost no traditional lectures like the ones at UCPH. Oral participation was a big part of most of my courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Traditional Customs of the Caucasus
Anthropology of Conflict
Anthropology of the Middle East and Islam
Israeli Minorities: Ethnicity, Gender and Religion
The Israeli-Palestinian Conflict
Territoriality of Radical Islamist Groups

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Israeli-Palestinian Conflict was my favourite class. The teacher was really good and it was a very contemporary class whcich was nice.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I liked going for walks in Petrin Park and visiting museums.
I went on a weekend trip to Český Krumlov, which was very nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes, it was, but at the same time I felt very separate from the Czech people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The local students mostly kept to themselves.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It seemed like the Czechs enjoyed going out to cafes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress too much about the exams. The teachers will change the exam format throughout the semester, and the teacher for each course chooses the exam formats themselves. 
There are no lunch spots or canteens on campus. 
Read the curriculum of the courses carefully, and ask the teachers if there is something you don't understand; they are very helpful.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It was nice to have a lot of different courses that are not available at UCPH.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I found it very difficult to find friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
